minutes.headline: Select Board honored two retiring members at their final meeting; routine appointments and contracts otherwise approved
minutes.summary: This was the final regular meeting for two outgoing select board members, Tom Alonzo and Michael Ray Jeff, who received legislative and police citations and gave farewell remarks. The board also ratified a new police officer and several seasonal/temporary appointments, approved a one-year FY2026 health insurance agreement, voted to co-sponsor a student-led townwide cleanup, created a bylaw review committee, and discussed (without a formal vote) not recharging the budget task force in favor of joint budget sessions with the school committee. Public comment raised concerns about the school budget override process, employee turmoil during budget season, and cemetery funding.

what_happened.line: The board leaned toward not recharging the budget task force, favoring joint budget sessions with the school committee instead
The board unanimously approved a one-year FY2026 health insurance agreement with the town's employee committee, running July 2025 through June 2026
This was the final regular meeting for two outgoing select board members, who received citations and gave farewell remarks
A resident said the board is not giving enough weight to a citizens petition appropriating school funds, contingent on a future override election
A resident argued cemetery capital work has gone underfunded for decades and cannot be sustained on the town's current plan

why_it_matters: How the town sets next year's school and town budget may shift from a standing task force to joint sessions between the select board and school committee -- a process change residents should watch for who is at the table.
The FY2026 health insurance agreement affects town employee costs and, by extension, the budget lines residents fund.
A citizens petition tied to a possible override election means residents may eventually be asked to vote on additional school funding.
